one_liner: SIMD range-based UTF-8 validator bundled in protobuf; edges out Lemire's SSE/NEON validator, mostly on ARM.
what_it_does: Checks whether a byte buffer is well-formed UTF-8 and, separately, returns the length of the longest valid UTF-8 prefix; it is what protobuf's C++/upb runtime uses internally to validate proto3 string fields. The C API is two functions: utf8_range_IsValid(data, len) and utf8_range_ValidPrefix(data, len). A thin C++ header, utf8_validity.h, wraps them as IsStructurallyValid()/SpanStructurallyValid() taking an absl::string_view. It is a validator only, not a decoder or UTF-8/UTF-16 transcoder.
how_it_is_fast: Core technique is the 'range algorithm': load 16 bytes, use a SIMD table lookup (NEON tbl / SSE pshufb) to assign each byte a predicted 'range index' based on where it should fall in a 1-4 byte UTF-8 sequence, then validate all 16 bytes against their [min,max] ranges in one pass, avoiding Lemire's more branch-heavy state tracking and the classic Hoehrmann DFA table walk. The shipped wrapper (utf8_range.c) adds an 8-bytes-at-a-time SWAR ASCII fast-skip (checking the high bit of 8 packed bytes at once) before entering the SIMD range check, and falls back to a naive byte-by-byte loop for tails under 16 bytes or on platforms without SSE4.1/ARM64 NEON.
when_to_use: Already depending on protobuf or Abseil in C/C++ and want its vendored validator instead of adding a new dependency
Buffers of roughly 1KB+ on ARMv8 NEON, where range2 shows its clearest edge over Lemire-style validation (~1.3x+)
ASCII-heavy input, where the wrapper's 8-byte SWAR ASCII skip dominates before SIMD is ever reached
Only need a boolean valid/invalid result or the longest-valid-prefix length, not decoding
x86-64 SSE4.1 targets where parity with a 2018-era SIMD validator is acceptable
when_not_to_use: Need AVX2/AVX-512 throughput: the shipped utf8_range.c only dispatches to SSE4.1 or 64-bit ARM NEON; range-avx2.c exists in the tree but is not wired into the wrapper protobuf actually links
Targeting 32-bit ARM, RISC-V, WASM, or other platforms without SSE4.1/NEON: falls back to a naive per-byte loop with no SIMD speedup
Small non-ASCII buffers: SSE4 numbers show range2 losing to Lemire at 32 bytes (2173 vs 2891 MB/s)
Need UTF-8<->UTF-16/32 transcoding, not just validation: this library only validates
Want current, independently-run benchmarks: the README table is an unmaintained ~2019 first-party benchmark against Lemire's 2018 prototype, not today's simdutf

integration.dependencies: none for the C library (utf8_range.c/.h); Abseil (absl::strings, for absl::string_view) for the C++ wrapper utf8_validity.h
integration.min_toolchain: C99/C11 for the core C file; C++ (protobuf's current C++17 baseline) for the wrapper; README's own build was tested with gcc-7.3, CMakeLists.txt requires CMake 3.16+
integration.platforms: x86-64 with SSE4.1, or aarch64 with NEON, for the SIMD path; any platform via a naive byte-by-byte fallback otherwise
integration.thread_safety: not documented, but both entry points are stateless pure functions over caller-owned buffers with no global/static mutable state, so concurrent calls on independent buffers are safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — Lemire's fastvalidate-utf-8 is a research prototype, not a library with a stable API, so there's no baseline API to drop into; utf8_range is a vendorable replacement for hand-rolled or DFA-table UTF-8 checks

gotchas: The README benchmark tables measure the original standalone research files (range-neon.c, range2-*.c, lemire-*.c via main.c), not utf8_range.c, the 2023 Google-rewritten wrapper with the ASCII fast path that protobuf actually ships and links
No AVX2 dispatch reaches production despite range-avx2.c sitting in the same directory — the wrapper only branches on __SSE4_1__ or __ARM_NEON+64-bit
Only static-library linkage is provided (CMake/Bazel add_library targets utf8_range and utf8_validity); a shared-library request (issue #14958) was closed without adding one
The component's own LICENSE file is MIT (Yibo Cai 2019 + Google 2022) even though the surrounding protobuf repo is BSD-3-Clause — relevant if vendoring just this directory
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only if you're already pulling in protobuf/Abseil and want its bundled C validator without adding a new dependency; simdutf8 (up to 23x over Rust std), SimdUnicode (up to 14x over .NET), and xutf (1.5-10x over simdutf) show larger and more current speedups, and utf8_range's own edge over Lemire is ARM-specific and within noise on x86 SSE4.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README benchmark (gcc-7.3, no optimization flags stated) compares 'range2' (a two-block NEON/SSE variant of the range algorithm) against Lemire's 2018 fastvalidate-utf-8 prototype on an unspecified ARMv8-A chip and an Intel Xeon E5-2650 (SSE4.1). On NEON, range2 beats Lemire by about 1.17x-1.78x depending on buffer size (~1.32x on the UTF-8 demo text and at 1K-1M buffers); on SSE4 it is within noise of Lemire (near parity on demo text and 1M, and slower than Lemire at 32 bytes).
status_note: Actively maintained as part of protobuf (this component last touched 2026-06-19; the protobuf repo overall as of 2026-09-25); MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor on its own, but only static-library builds are supported.
